title: Digital Asset Securities Control Principles
license_note: DASCP is a third-party copyrighted white paper (DTCC, Clearstream, Euroclear, in collaboration with BCG, May 2024). This file uses DASCP ids, official titles, and short paraphrased descriptions in our own words for interoperability between BPO and the DASCP framework. For the authoritative prose consult the source. Risk-to-control attributions follow the white paper's appendix and were cross-checked against the consolidated control-card figure on its page 14. Where the appendix grouped multiple risks under a shared Controls column (p.26 R2/R3; p.34 R20/R21) the per-link attribution required a subject-matter split; those specific links carry an inline `note` documenting the judgment and the p.14 cross-check.

principles.title: Legal Certainty
principles.description: Operations comply with applicable laws and regulations so that market integrity and investor confidence are preserved.

principles.title: Regulatory Compliance
principles.description: Alignment with regulatory frameworks underpins trust and safety in digital asset markets.

principles.title: Resilience and Security
principles.description: Infrastructure resists disruption, protects sensitive data, and maintains continuous operation of digital asset services.

principles.title: Safeguarding Customer Assets
principles.description: Smart-contract governance protects customer assets within the digital asset ecosystem.

principles.title: Connectivity and Interoperability
principles.description: Transactions and settlement flow across diverse networks, enabling the seamless transfer and settlement of digital asset securities.

principles.title: Operational Scalability
principles.description: Standardized roles and smart-contract functions deliver efficiency and cost-effectiveness as the market grows.

risks.title: Digital Asset Legal Noncompliance
risks.description: Loss or damages from failing to comply with the rapidly evolving global legal standards governing digital assets, including jurisdictional divergence and integration of digital and conventional asset frameworks.

risks.title: Unclear Settlement Finality
risks.description: Settlement finality is not achieved or the settlement status of a transaction is unclear.

risks.title: Smart Contract Legal Enforceability
risks.description: Differences in legal status, recognition, and enforceability of smart contracts across jurisdictions affect cross-border transactions and asset custody.

risks.title: Unauthorized Investor Holdings
risks.description: Regulatory or financial harm if a non-compliant or unauthorized investor holds or transfers a digital asset security (e.g. accreditation, caps), excluding AML/CTF.

risks.title: Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risks
risks.description: Platform misuse to obscure illicit funds or finance terrorism due to inadequate AML/CTF controls (KYC, transaction monitoring, reporting).

risks.title: DLT Network Suitability / Adaptability
risks.description: The DLT network may be unsuitable or unable to track evolving technological standards and regulations governing digital asset securities.

risks.title: Digital Asset Regulatory Noncompliance
risks.description: Securities are non-compliant with potentially conflicting jurisdictional and asset-class securities regulations.

risks.title: Dispute Resolution
risks.description: Decentralized DLT governance can hinder predictable dispute resolution across networks.

risks.title: Market Abuse
risks.description: Insufficient surveillance to prevent market manipulation and uphold transparent, fair-market integrity.

risks.title: Network Integrity
risks.description: The integrity of the DLT network is compromised, e.g. via attacks, consensus issues, or supermajority-node manipulation.

risks.title: Network Traffic Attack
risks.description: The DLT network is unavailable due to traffic-based attacks such as DDoS.

risks.title: Smart Contract Integrity
risks.description: Smart-contract integrity on the DLT network is compromised by code defects or vulnerable external libraries.

risks.title: Compromised Inter-Network Transfer
risks.description: Inter-network (cross-ledger) asset-transfer integrity is compromised.

risks.title: Poisoned Oracle
risks.description: Off-chain data is tampered with via a compromised oracle (poisoned-oracle scenario).

risks.title: Private Data Leakage
risks.description: Customers' personal data or proprietary data is leaked or stolen.

risks.title: Exploited Consensus Algorithm
risks.description: The consensus mechanism is exploited, leading to unauthorized transfers, censorship, double-spending, or operational disruption of validation.

risks.title: Quantum Computing Threat
risks.description: Quantum computing breaks asymmetric encryption, recovering private keys from public keys.

risks.title: Interoperability Security Risks
risks.description: Security vulnerabilities arise from connecting the platform to other blockchain networks or traditional financial systems.

risks.title: Network Outage
risks.description: A single event (disaster, common failure point, pervasive issue) incapacitates multiple critical components, nodes, or networks, causing extensive disruption.

risks.title: Smart Contract Defects
risks.description: DLT smart contracts cease to operate correctly because of software bugs or defects.

risks.title: Complexity of Change Management
risks.description: DLT's decentralized, immutable nature complicates feature deployment, smart-contract updates, and patching of vulnerabilities, hindering timely adaptation.

risks.title: Operational Errors
risks.description: Errors, failures, or bottlenecks across the security life cycle arise when smart-contract code does not conform to standard market practice.

risks.title: Asset Mismanagement
risks.description: Digital assets are lost, stolen, or erroneously transferred due to operational, system, or protocol weaknesses in asset management.

risks.title: Immutable Transactions
risks.description: Immutability prevents reversing errors or returning securities to their original owners after a processing issue.

risks.title: Inadequate Managerial Oversight
risks.description: Operations are compromised by insufficiently qualified management or weak governance structures, creating operational and regulatory exposure.

risks.title: Asset Misappropriation
risks.description: Digital asset securities are misappropriated via code vulnerabilities, unauthorized intermediary actions, or fraudulent misuse of access privileges.

risks.title: Unauthorized Smart Contract Access
risks.description: Unauthorized manipulation or exploitation of smart-contract functions via technical vulnerabilities, weak access controls, or compromised security protocols.

risks.title: Insufficient Smart Contract Control
risks.description: A custodian or intermediary lacks the necessary control over digital asset securities, tokens, or smart-contract functions.

risks.title: Financial Institution Insolvency
risks.description: A broker-dealer or custodian becomes insolvent without protections ensuring customer assets are bankruptcy-remote.

risks.title: Interoperability Risk
risks.description: Integrating digital assets with traditional financial systems and multiple blockchain architectures (public, public-permissioned, private) to ensure seamless transactions across the financial spectrum.

risks.title: Network Utilization and Fragmentation
risks.description: A digital-assets platform's operational viability declines because user engagement and transaction volume are too low.

risks.title: Inability to Scale
risks.description: DLT networks fail to scale to growing transaction volume, degrading post-trade capture, throughput, and reliability.

risks.title: Digital Asset Liquidity
risks.description: Rapid, large liquidity shifts in digital-asset markets, possibly amplified by real-time settlement, threaten market stability.

risks.title: Reputational Risk
risks.description: DLT's newness and association with high-profile controversies enhance reputational risk from misunderstanding or misuse.

risks.title: Market Inefficiency
risks.description: Structural or implementation frictions cause disparities between intrinsic value and market pricing, enabling undue arbitrage.

risks.title: Inadequate Stakeholder / Client Understanding of Digital Asset Securities
risks.description: Insufficient education and training programs leave stakeholders and clients unable to understand the technology, regulation, and operations specific to digital asset securities.

controls.title: Participation Guidelines
controls.description: Fair, open, risk-based criteria for users and third-party service providers permitted to participate, including due diligence and ongoing compliance monitoring tailored to digital-asset markets.

controls.title: Product Eligibility
controls.description: Clear standards and requirements for supported product types, including due diligence for new listings and ongoing disclosure to maintain regulatory compliance.

controls.title: Network and Oracle Vetting
controls.description: Thorough checks on network and oracle alignment with DLT standards and governance before integration; rigorous validation of reliability and security SLAs.

controls.title: Participant Roles, Responsibilities, and Obligations
controls.description: Clearly defined and documented service-participant roles, responsibilities, and obligations, integrating geographic and identity nuances to align with jurisdictional standards.

mitigates_risks.note: Appendix p.26 lists R2 (Unclear Settlement Finality) and R3 (Smart Contract Legal Enforceability) under a shared Controls column; attributed to R3 by subject-matter (smart-contract enforceability) and corroborated by the control-card figure on p.14.

controls.title: Service Providers' Responsibilities / Limitation of Liability
controls.description: Clearly documented roles, responsibilities, and obligations of service providers covering both legal and operational aspects, with explicit limitations of liability.

controls.title: Terms and Conditions
controls.description: Legal basis for a service via rules or contractual agreements binding service provider and stakeholders, with parameters for transfer, custody, and control of assets consistent with applicable law.

controls.title: Governance
controls.description: Clear governance arrangements detailing oversight and management of the service.

controls.title: Rule Enforcement and Arrangements
controls.description: Effective monitoring and enforcement of rules with authority to discipline, limit, suspend, or terminate participant activities and to halt or resume specific-asset transactions as needed.

controls.title: Regulatory Approval and Oversight
controls.description: All required rule filings, no-action relief, or regulatory approvals and notifications completed prior to implementation.

controls.title: Asset Safeguarding and Segregation
controls.description: Stringent controls ensuring customer assets are safeguarded and segregated from the custodian's or broker-dealer's own assets, preventing commingling and misuse.

controls.title: Policies and Procedures
controls.description: Comprehensive policies and procedures across business and IT functions (including blockchain management and smart-contract deployment), with regular testing — simulations, stress tests, security audits — kept current with technology and regulation.

controls.title: Education and Training for Stakeholders on Digital Asset Securities
controls.description: Comprehensive education and training programs covering fundamentals of digital assets, underlying technologies, regulatory compliance, risk factors, and best practices.

controls.title: Smart Contract Auditing Guidelines
controls.description: Guidelines for auditing smart contracts as machine-executable legal agreements, verifying both legal compliance and enforceability of their terms under applicable legal frameworks.

mitigates_risks.note: Appendix p.26 lists R2 (Unclear Settlement Finality) and R3 (Smart Contract Legal Enforceability) under a shared Controls column; attributed to R3 by subject-matter (smart-contract enforceability) and corroborated by the control-card figure on p.14.

controls.title: Certification
controls.description: Where smart contracts are deployed across networks governed by different parties, a defined process lets a trusted party validate the integrity of a given smart contract.

mitigates_risks.note: Appendix p.26 lists R2 (Unclear Settlement Finality) and R3 (Smart Contract Legal Enforceability) under a shared Controls column; attributed to R3 by subject-matter (smart-contract enforceability) and corroborated by the control-card figure on p.14.

controls.title: Investor Compliance and Access Control
controls.description: Mechanisms (allow-lists, verifiable credentials, etc.) that only allow authorized investors in good compliance standing (KYC, sanctions, etc.) to hold registered securities.

controls.title: Multiparty Transaction Validation
controls.description: Collaborative validation mechanism requiring approvals from multiple authorized parties, with periodic updates to address emerging security challenges.

controls.title: Dispute Resolution Mechanism
controls.description: Dispute-resolution mechanism with clear escalation paths and consistent outcomes across DLT networks.

controls.title: Code Auditing
controls.description: All smart-contract code tested for vulnerabilities, bugs, performance issues, or defects by an independent third-party auditor.

mitigates_risks.note: Appendix p.34 lists R20 (Smart Contract Defects) and R21 (Change Management) under a shared Controls column; attributed to R20 by subject-matter (defect detection / recovery) and corroborated by the control-card figure on p.14.

controls.title: Smart Contract Entitlements
controls.description: Access to smart-contract data and functions restricted to standard roles using fine-grained entitlements.

controls.title: Quantum-Resistant Signature Algorithms
controls.description: Implement a quantum-resistant signature algorithm with periodic audits of the algorithm choices to maintain efficacy against quantum threats.

controls.title: Intraoperability between DLT Networks
controls.description: Adhere to industry-accepted cross-network communication protocols for blockchain interoperability — asset representation, transaction formats, data exchange — for seamless, secure interactions across platforms.

controls.title: Token Specification Model
controls.description: Define smart-contract requirements through a human-readable markup language modelling smart-contract specifications, understandable by business, operations, and IT personas.

controls.title: Data / Properties
controls.description: Data properties embedded in smart contracts conform to recognized nomenclature and conventions, identifying and describing the security and supporting life-cycle event processing.

controls.title: Functions / Behaviors
controls.description: Conform to a common set of functions, behaviours, and SLAs supporting security life-cycle operations such as issuance and settlement.

controls.title: Bookkeeping
controls.description: Conform to an accounting model supporting both private and public securities, adapted to comply with international digital-asset-securities reporting standards.

controls.title: Account Structure
controls.description: Conform to a common model for investor accounts delineating customer vs proprietary accounts with appropriate attribution.

controls.title: Key Life Cycle Management
controls.description: Secure multi-party cryptographic system covering full key life cycle — generation, distribution, storage, destruction — with reviews and updates to adapt to emerging threats.

controls.title: Smart Contract Roles
controls.description: Standard roles defining who can access smart-contract data and functions.

controls.title: Emergency Stop
controls.description: Embedded kill-switch or halt process for smart contracts, accessible only by a role with elevated permissions.

controls.title: Account Pause
controls.description: Ability to freeze or pause activity for a given investor or wallet, controlled by the investor's agent or a role with elevated permissions.

controls.title: Token Pause
controls.description: Ability to freeze or pause activity for all or some of the token inventory, controlled by the investor's agent or a role with elevated permissions.

controls.title: Audit Trail
controls.description: Comprehensive, synchronously time-stamped record of on-chain and relevant off-chain digital-asset events and transactions, supporting full-system recovery and verification.

controls.title: Data Life Cycle Management
controls.description: Documented and managed process for data collection, usage, transfer, storage, security, retention, and deletion.

controls.title: Data Subject Access Rights Enforcement
controls.description: Privileged roles able to access, amend, or erase a data subject's data on request, with appropriate oversight arrangements.

controls.title: Event Monitoring and Alerts
controls.description: Real-time monitoring and audit of operations with automatic alerts on predefined thresholds for prompt detection of anomalies and deviations from standard procedures.

controls.title: Redundancy and Concurrency
controls.description: Technology resilience measures preventing a single point of failure from loss of a major node or all nodes in a geographic region.

controls.title: Backups
controls.description: Regularly record and store copies of the ledger and service-related data to prevent loss of data integrity or availability from destruction or corruption.

controls.title: Failure Prevention, Detection, and Recovery
controls.description: Processes for detecting failures and seamlessly transitioning to backup systems to prevent disruption, including reporting, recovering, and resolving multiple failure types.

mitigates_risks.note: Appendix p.34 lists R20 (Smart Contract Defects) and R21 (Change Management) under a shared Controls column; attributed to R20 by subject-matter (defect detection / recovery) and corroborated by the control-card figure on p.14.

controls.title: Recovery Testing
controls.description: Regular simulation and validation of recovery processes to confirm the system can restore data accurately and securely after unexpected incidents.

controls.title: Private Data Segregation
controls.description: Segregate and restrict access to confidential data — personal, client, and firm proprietary — that should not be broadly available on the network.

controls.title: Anonymization and Pseudonymization
controls.description: Anonymize or pseudonymize sensitive data to protect individual or entity privacy.

controls.title: Identity Verification
controls.description: System or process for verifying client identities and compliance status — internal mechanisms, third-party services, or other methods.

controls.title: Geographical Distribution
controls.description: Strategically distribute data across diverse geographic locations within regulatory boundaries to minimize the impact of regional disruptions.

controls.title: Feature Deployment Process
controls.description: Processes for deploying new features or updates that minimize disruption and preserve network integrity.

mitigates_risks.note: Appendix p.34 lists R20 (Smart Contract Defects) and R21 (Change Management) under a shared Controls column; attributed to R21 by subject-matter (change management) and corroborated by the control-card figure on p.14.

controls.title: Data Integrity Correction
controls.description: Privileged roles able to edit and modify data to maintain accuracy, consistency, and reliability of financial records.

controls.title: Data Lineage
controls.description: Comprehensive data-lineage process tracking transaction and data-process journeys from origin through all transformations and uses to final state.

controls.description: Track shared data and reconcile or balance inventory across networks.

controls.title: Compliance and Policy Management
controls.description: Implement and enforce transaction policies consistently across all networks, with mechanisms to verify and record compliance per transaction.

controls.title: Continuous Management Education
controls.description: Ongoing training programs for management in digital-asset security and regulatory compliance, including fit-and-proper tests to strengthen oversight.

controls.title: Legacy Infrastructure Integration
controls.description: Method or abstraction layer enabling users to access their security holdings via classic or new DLT infrastructure.

controls.title: Third-Party Integration Guidelines
controls.description: Rigorous guidelines for third-party service integration to maintain security across interconnected platforms.

controls.title: Community Engagement Framework
controls.description: Stakeholder collaboration program with forums and channels for feedback, issue reporting, and collaborative problem-solving, establishing best practices through active feedback.

controls.title: Liquidity Management Strategies
controls.description: Strategies to actively manage digital-asset liquidity to meet demand across market conditions, with regular stress testing of liquidity-pool robustness.
